observations: Clear establishing aerial of the zoo buildings, paths, ponds and surrounding neighborhood. Title and attribution are readable.

Previously failing park region is corrected: continuous green ground covers the broad waterfront and inland park areas, with paths and shoreline paving remaining distinct.
No recurrence of the large white landcover omission is visible.
Previously failing harbor entrance and peninsula now have green park cover bounded by clear paths, roads, shore edges and water.
Harbor slips, boats and breakwater geometry remain coherent after the correction.
Previously failing Belmont/harbor frontage retains continuous green park cover, planting and mapped paths, without disconnected green islands in broad pale terrain.
Water and pier framing remain unobstructed.
The camera turns inland toward Wrigley through the neighborhood. A nearby tower naturally occupies the right foreground without blocking the destination or showing a clipped camera intersection.
Wrigley is recognizable ahead among the neighborhood blocks; open field and seating bowl establish the arrival.
Clear aerial view into the open ballpark shows the irregular field, stands and light frames. Rear faces of the outfield boards are naturally visible from this side.
Final southwest arrival clearly frames the red marquee, open ballpark, blue boards and Gallagher lawn.
Marquee lettering, route title and bottom map attribution remain readable; the neighboring foreground roof does not block the landmark.

No conspicuous corrupted frame, unintended camera obstruction or clipped typography is apparent in the sampled images.
The final arrival clearly presents the marquee, field, seating bowl and surrounding Wrigleyville context.
The title and OpenStreetMap attribution are readable in all ten sampled frames.
